practice: What does archaeological context include?
A find's recorded location, layer and relationships
Only its display colour
Only the name given to a teaching picture
A complete biography of every ancient person
Two similar objects have different recorded settings. What should an investigator do?
Study each setting rather than assume identical histories
Erase the location records because the objects look similar
Give both the same age without checking
Use a photograph as a complete replacement for context
Which site in this lesson is on Palawan?
Tabon
Callao
Both are in Cagayan
Neither is an archaeological site
A card lists stone tools and Homo sapiens remains at Tabon. Which comparison is useful?
Tools and remains can answer different questions about past life
A tool is another name for a human bone
Every object at one site must have one age
The site name proves a complete family tree
Which species name is associated with the Callao fossils described in 2019?
Homo luzonensis
Homo sapiens as another name for Homo luzonensis
A modern community name chosen from appearance
A name for all stone tools
A learner sees 2019 on a Callao research report and calls it the age of the fossils. What should improve?
Distinguish the report date from the ancient material's age
Give every fossil the publication year as its age
Move Callao to Palawan to match the report
Treat the report as a complete account of every family
With years ago, which number refers to farther in the past?
2,000 years ago compared with 1,000 years ago
1,000 years ago compared with 2,000 years ago
Both expressions mean the same age
Neither can describe an age
Fictional find C is 2,000 to 3,000 years old and D is 2,500 to 3,500. Which interval overlaps?
2,500 to 3,000 years ago
1,000 to 1,500 years ago
3,500 to 4,000 years ago
The numbers show no overlap
What does a saved Evidence Journal clue represent?
A learning reference to authored information
Ownership of an original fossil
Permission to excavate a cave
A reward made from human remains
A museum uses a teaching drawing beside a site explanation. Which label is honest?
Teaching illustration, not an original find
Original fossil merely because it is in a lesson
Photograph of an ancient person's exact life
Proof that all people had one ancestor
retries: Which record best preserves archaeological context?
Location, layer and the relationship to nearby finds
Only a cleaned object with its place forgotten
Only the colour chosen for a poster
A guess about the person who owned it
A source identifies Homo sapiens remains at Tabon. What can the label support?
Our species was present at that site long ago
Callao and Tabon must be the same cave
Every nearby object has the same exact age
The remains identify every living person's ancestor
How are the Tabon and Callao cards different?
They name different locations and species identifications
They are two names for one modern city
They show every ancient route between islands
They record the exact life of every person represented
A museum label says a study was published in 2019. What does that date identify?
When the research description was published
The exact year every fossil formed
The first arrival of people on all islands
The age of every object from the cave
Someone wants to remove a possible find to take a closer photo. Which plan better protects the record?
Leave it in place and ask responsible site staff for guidance
Move it first and guess its location later
Wash it to make it easier to display
Offer it as a classroom prize
